findings.why_it_matters: A reader of the transcription sees the exception list cut off at 'rules 2 through' and a stray '5.' item, so the scope of the qualification exceptions (rules 2 through 5) is not stated in one place and the text looks like a sixth-rule sub-list.
findings.pdf_says: uniqueness shall then be established through qualification for each user-defined name explicitly referenced, except as specified in rules 2 through 5.  All available qualifiers need not be specified so long as uniqueness is established.
findings.markdown_says:
uniqueness shall then be established through qualification for each user-defined name explicitly referenced, except as specified in rules 2 through

   5\. All available qualifiers need not be specified so long as uniqueness is established.
findings.explanation: The printed line break inside the sentence 'except as specified in rules 2 through 5.' was turned into a paragraph break, so the cross-reference reads 'rules 2 through' (incomplete) and the remainder starts a new paragraph beginning '5\.', which renders as if it were a list item numbered 5 inside rule 6. The sentence should be one paragraph ending '...rules 2 through 5. All available qualifiers...'.
